svg.title: The three destinations a raw reasoning trace must be kept out of
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure. A lifecycle strip across the top runs from generated, to used for this answer, to summarised or dropped, to forgotten, with a note that traces are ephemeral by default. Below, three cards name the destinations a trace must not reach and why each fails differently. In the next turn's prompt, traces are long and noisy and discarded hypotheses read like conclusions, so the next turn can treat a rejected branch as an accepted fact; carry the answer and decisions instead. In the cached prefix, thinking is freshly generated every call, so a trace inside the prefix breaks it and every downstream call reverts to a full-price miss; keep the reasoning segment strictly after the stable material. In long-term memory, a trace is verbose and low-signal and risks persisting a discarded line of reasoning as a learned fact; persist the outcome, never the deliberation.
svg.text: Three places a reasoning trace must not end up
A raw trace is a working note. It exists to produce this turn's answer, and its job ends there.
generated
used for this answer
summarised or dropped
forgotten
Ephemeral by default. Keeping a distilled version needs a specific, audited reason — debugging and evaluation are legitimate ones.
The next turn's prompt
what goes wrong
Traces are long and noisy. Discarded
hypotheses read, out of context, like
conclusions, so the next turn can treat a
rejected branch as an accepted fact.
instead
Carry the answer and any decisions it
produced. Summarise the reasoning to a
short note, or drop it.
The cached prefix
what goes wrong
Thinking is freshly generated on every
call and different every time. A trace
inside the prefix breaks it, and every
downstream call reverts to a full-price
miss.
instead
Keep the reasoning segment strictly after
the stable material: system prompt, tools,
pinned context.
Long-term memory
what goes wrong
Verbose and low-signal, and it risks
persisting a discarded line of reasoning
as though it were a learned fact.
instead
Persist the outcome — the decision, the
preference, the corrected rule — never the
deliberation behind it.
A trace is the highest-volume, lowest-durability content in the whole context, which makes it the first thing to shrink or clear.
Log it to a side channel if you need it for debugging. That is a different destination from the live context.
